idiom_name: frozen legacy interface type + explicit mapper functions
implementation_notes: TypeScript's structural types make the legacy contract an ordinary interface declaration - the old wire DTO - so the compiler can point at every consumer of the old shape and fail the build when code reaches for a field the legacy client never sends. The window itself is a mapper module with explicit toLegacy()/fromLegacy() functions, and a /** @deprecated */ JSDoc tag on the frozen declarations surfaces the intent in editors, which TypeScript honours in completion lists and suggestion diagnostics. Nothing is enforced at runtime, though: types are erased, so the mapping and its validation still have to be written and are what actually protects the old client.
pitfalls: @deprecated is editor-level only: it neither fails the build nor blocks an import, so the migration also needs a lint rule or an import boundary.
Types are erased at runtime, so a payload that satisfies the interface at compile time can still be wrong (numbers arriving as strings); validate at the boundary.
Optional versus absent is a wire-level distinction: 'ccy?: string' allows undefined, the client may send the key explicitly, and only the payload decides which one is correct.
